- K2, price plus macro: 0.34 is at the 21st percentile (historical median 0.41, p10-p90 0.28-0.53), and the nearest distance is at the 11th. Today's macro state is matched better than a typical historical risk-off day.
- K3, adding gold: 0.48 is at the 64th percentile (p10-p90 0.31-0.58), an ordinary match.
The gold part holds: gold63 (z -2.25) is the largest average contributor to the K3 picks' distances (27%) and the largest for 4 of the 10 picks. But the nearest K3 match, 2008-09-05, matched gold closely (z gap 0.44, 5% of its distance).
verdicts.corrected: Today's price state (K1, 18th percentile) and price-plus-macro state (K2, 21st percentile) are both matched better than a typical historical risk-off day. With gold added, match quality is ordinary (64th percentile). Only the 63-day gold fall is extreme (0.9th percentile; 27% of K3 distance).

issues: The union keeps the earliest date in each 60-day cluster, which is not neutral. It measures from the start of each risk-off spell (median 9 days risk-off vs 23 today). It puts the union F3 and F2 12m medians (+18.4% / +15.8%) below the 5th percentile of 500 random date choices (F3 range +21.5% to +29.6%, F2 +16.7% to +22.0%) and the re-entry median (21 days) above their 95th percentile (18). The headline F2/F3 medians and the comparison 'about QQQ's +22%' inherit this bias. 8 of the 9 individual sets have a higher F3 median than the union.

The union is not a set of states like today's. 10 of its 29 dates fail the R2 price-state filter on their own date (cluster age under 10 days, vol20 at or below 25%, or drawdown outside -8% to -20%). 11 of 29 had risk-off spells that ended before reaching today's 23 days.

The episodes are not independent. The 28 union episodes with 12m outcomes form only 15 clusters of non-overlapping 12m windows: 1996-98 has 5 episodes, and 2007-08, 2011-12 and 2022 have 3 each. All Wilson intervals computed at n=28 are too narrow; for example, the cluster-level bear rate is 5/15 (Wilson 15-58%).

'n_distinct_runs' counts runs of the ELIG mask, which breaks whenever NDX closes above the EMA mid-week. The bootstrap and empirical pools actually come from 94 (B1), 26 (B3) and 39 (B4) distinct risk-off spells, not the ~141, ~54 and ~75 'runs' cited in the table and caveats.

Split halves of the union (1988-2006 vs 2007-2026) disagree: NDX 12m median +32.5% vs +18.2%; F3 beat QQQ in 50% vs 75%; whipsaw share 42% vs 75%; bear rate 17% vs 38%. The pooled figures average two different regimes.

C7 quotes the rising-yield statistic at 6 months, where it looks bad, and only because of 2022. At 12 months, the horizon used everywhere else, the rising-yield median is higher (F3 +31.6% vs +22.5%). Excluding 2022, the rising-yield 6m loss rate is lower than the risk-off average (7.3% vs 9.1%).

The analog selection hides a second, small loss mode: whipsaw years with flat bonds. Risk-off days with negative 12m F3/F2 returns occur in 1993 (35 of 40 days), 2000, 2001, 2004, 2006 and 2007, not only 2022. Six non-2022 spell starts lost 1.3-4.8% over 12m.

The 2022 worst case depends on the start date. F3 12m: -15.2% from 2022-01-07 (the spell start), -10.9% from 01-28, -7.2% from 02-09, -4.8% from 02-14 (F2: -14.3%, -10.4%, -7.9%, -5.7%). The reported minima understate the worst nearby start by about 4pp.

Recommendation 4 overstates the analog evidence for IEF over TLT. The positive counts differ by one episode (22/28 vs 21/28), and TLT had the higher mean (+7.2% vs +6.2%) and upper quartile (+18.4% vs +12.2%). Only the 2022 minimum (-23.4% vs -10.2%) favours IEF. The case for IEF rests on the audit's full-backtest 2022 result, not on these analogs.

The OOS outcome partly reflects the calendar of the weekly rule. The exit came on the first below-EMA close (2026-10-16), which happened to be a Friday. The two later re-crosses above the EMA (10-19..21 and 10-27..29) ended one or two days before a Friday mark, so there was no re-entry and second exit. Measured from the 10-06 record, F3 is -17.2% vs NDX -13.5% (see C2).

No code bugs were found. A re-run of analogs.py with its output redirected reproduces analogs.json byte-for-byte (md5 9190b2bf23a614fa076377ae11175814), and a recompute directly from common.py matches the 2022 and OOS figures. This review evaluated 23 alternative definitions: 6 union date rules (including the random-date draw), 3 spell-based sets, 4 half-splits, 4 rising-yield conditionings and 6 bootstrap block settings.

result.headline: Choosing 2x or 3x sets how much risk you take. It does not change efficiency: at matched drawdown or volatility the two are tied within about 1pp/yr. So keep 2x (QLD, vol target 0.30); 3x's extra ~4.4pp/yr is payment for much fatter drawdown tails. The biggest realism finding is new: rebalancing on Friday beat a timing-luck-free 5-weekday tranche by ~2.5pp/yr (F2). Plan on ~17%/-28% for F2 in-sample, not 19.7%/-24%. Execute at the Friday pre-close with market-on-close orders, using a 2pp no-trade band that always trades on/off switches.

claims.claim: The leverage level sets the drawdown band; the vol target only fine-tunes it. 2x tops out at about 20% CAGR because its NDX exposure is capped at 1.70x.
claims.evidence: IS 1988-01-01..2026-07-24, gold_phys 15%, IEF off-leg. 1x: maxDD -19.0..-19.4%, CAGR 10.9-13.0%, Sharpe 1.16-1.19. 2x vt .15-.35: DD -23.2..-25.1%, CAGR 16.2-19.9%, Sharpe 1.02-1.04. 3x vt .15-.45: DD -29.1..-43.8%, CAGR 21.5-26.8%, Sharpe 0.95-0.97. Going from 2x vt .30 to vt .45 adds +0.34pp CAGR but -6.3pp DD (20.05%/-30.3%), and that point is Pareto-dominated by F3 (24.13%/-30.0%). Pareto set IS: qqq vt.30-.45, qld vt.15-.35, all tqqq.

claims.claim: '2x preferred' is confirmed only as a risk-level choice. At matched risk, 2x and 3x are statistically tied. Matching on the realized maxDD gives opposite answers depending on the drawdown level, because each family must use an off-design vol target to reach the other's drawdown.
claims.evidence: Timing-luck-free tranche, IS, CAGR at equal maxDD (2x vs 3x): 25%: 14.2 vs 13.9; 30%: 17.4 vs 17.8. At equal vol 15%: 14.2 vs 14.2. Bootstrap-matched (Friday), at equal median maxDD 25%: 15.8 vs 15.4; 30%: 19.1 vs 17.5; at equal 1-in-20 maxDD 40%: 18.9 vs 17.2. Realized Friday path: at DD -24%, 2x 19.72% vs 3x 14.90% (needs vt 0.075); at DD -30%, 3x 24.12% vs 2x 20.05% (needs vt 0.44). Frontier owner IS: 2x for DD 20-28%, 3x for 29%+.

claims.claim: F3's extra return comes from the exposure cap, not a worse instrument. Holding TQQQ at 2/3 weight (identical NDX exposure to F2) was slightly cheaper than QLD historically, but that advantage reversed after 2023.
claims.evidence: F3 - F2 IS: +4.42pp CAGR, -6.0pp DD (bootstrap 95% [+1.83,+7.55]). Exposure-cap effect (F3 vs TQQQx2/3 vt.30): +3.87pp CAGR, -5.3pp DD. Instrument effect (TQQQx2/3 - QLD): +0.55pp IS [+0.15,+0.97] (H1 +0.63, H2 +0.48). With real ETFs 2010-03..freeze: +0.43pp; 2023..latest: -0.41pp/yr.

claims.claim: 3x carries much fatter drawdown tails and more single-day gap risk at the exposure cap.
claims.evidence: Paired block bootstrap (1000 draws, 63-day blocks, IS), F2 vs F3: median maxDD -30.9% vs -40.9%; 1-in-20 maxDD -41.8% vs -54.3%; P(DD worse than -50%) 0.8% vs 11.1%; P(Calmar F2 > F3) 0.83. A one-day -20% NDX gap at the cap costs -34% (F2) vs -51% (F3). Worst IS day -11.0% vs -13.9%; worst 5 days -15.8% vs -20.4%.

claims.claim: The rebalance weekday matters a lot, and Friday (the research convention) is the best of the five in-sample. The edge holds in both halves, in most years, and again out-of-sample, and there is a plausible weekend mechanism.
claims.evidence: F2 lag1 IS CAGR/maxDD: Mon 14.47/-33.2, Tue 16.87/-31.4, Wed 17.81/-28.3, Thu 16.86/-27.1, Fri 19.71/-24.0, daily 15.68/-29.6. F3: 16.95, 20.29, 21.84, 19.94, 24.13; daily 18.97. Fri minus mean of the other four: +3.10pp [+0.98,+5.18] (F2) and +4.17pp [+1.41,+7.00] (F3), p about 0.002. Friday wins 29/39 years (F2); H1 +3.8pp, H2 +2.6pp. OOS Jul25-Nov17 2026 (F2): Fri -6.0% vs Mon..Thu -9.4/-13.2/-12.9/-12.2%. Friday sampling has fewer on/off switches (189 vs 215-217). Mechanism: after a Friday close below EMA-100, the next session averages -11.8bp (H1) / -21.3bp (H2); after a Monday close below it, Tuesday averages +8.3 / +65.4bp (t 4.2).

claims.claim: Timing-luck-free planning numbers (5 equal tranches, one rebalanced each weekday) sit well below the Friday headline.

Trading one day late (lag 2) looks costly on Fridays, but that cost comes almost entirely from 1988-2006 and from the Friday effect. Averaged over weekdays, a one-day delay costs only about 0.2-0.3pp/yr. Delay still leaves weekend crash exposure.
claims.evidence: F2 lag1 to lag2: 19.71% to 18.28%, DD -24.0% to -25.1%, Calmar 0.82 to 0.73 (H1 -3.13pp, H2 +0.19pp). F3: 24.13% to 22.24%, DD -30.0% to -35.0%, Calmar 0.80 to 0.63 (H1 -4.35, H2 +0.54). Lag cost averaged over the 5 weekday phases: F2 0.17pp (H1 0.12, H2 0.19); F3 0.27pp. Oct-1987 stress (before START): F2 lag2 -16.9% vs lag1 -4.0%, and on 19-Oct-87 -12.6% vs +0.5%; F3 -27.2% vs -9.3%.

claims.claim: How holiday Fridays are handled is immaterial. Computing the signal a day early (Thursday close, trade Friday) is the worst option.
claims.evidence: mark_wk (trade the week's last trading day) vs Friday-only marks: F2 19.56% vs 19.71% (DD -24.0% both); F3 23.82% vs 24.13% (DD -32.6% vs -30.0%; only 75 days differ, which shows how path-sensitive maxDD is). Thursday-signal/Friday-trade: F2 15.62% / -30.0%; F3 18.11% / -37.6%.

claims.claim: No-trade bands cut the number of trades and orders sharply, with no measurable effect on returns. They barely reduce turnover, which comes from structural sources (regime switches, choppy-market flips, Aug/Sep halving). A pure 10pp band skips some risk-off switches, so an override is needed.
claims.evidence: My own drift-faithful loop, F2, 10 bps, IS. Band 0/2/5/10pp: CAGR 18.59/18.61/18.52/18.43%; rebalances/yr 50.4/18.8/16.4/16.0; orders/yr 132/56/49/48; turnover/yr 12.86/12.60/12.50/12.43. Band 2pp vs 0: +0.02pp [-0.06,+0.12] (F2), -0.07pp [-0.20,+0.05] (F3). F3 pure 10pp band skipped 4 risk-off switches (DD -31.6%); with the override, 0. At an assumed $1/order fixed fee on a $60k account: 22 bps/yr (band 0) vs 9 bps/yr (2pp).

claims.claim: Turnover of about 12.5x per year makes all-in trading cost the main controllable drag: roughly -1.5pp CAGR per 10 bps. Approximating weekly drift with constant weights costs only 0.05-0.13pp.
claims.evidence: Drift loop, band 0, IS CAGR at 0/3/10/20 bps: F2 20.12/19.66/18.59/17.07%; F3 24.46/24.00/22.93/21.41%. Constant-weight engine vs drift at 3 bps: F2 19.71 vs 19.66; F3 24.13 vs 24.00. My drift loop reproduces main_drift_check exactly (FULL: F3 23.482% / -29.58%; F2 19.294% / -24.05%).

claims.claim: Backtests on real ETFs beat the pure simulations over 2010+, so the sims are not flattering. The exceptions are rate-shock years, where the treasury synthetics understate losses, and the current high-rate regime, where TQQQ trails its sim.
claims.evidence: 2010-03..freeze. F2-IEF: real 18.75% vs sim 18.17% (TE 1.60%), maxDD -24.0% vs -22.5%. F3-IEF: 25.67% vs 24.83% (TE 1.89%). Real minus sim (pp), F2/F3: 2020 +1.7/+2.2; 2022 -1.6/-1.6; 2025 +0.3/+0.1; 2026 YTD -0.2/-0.5; OOS -0.2/-0.4. Sleeves: TQQQ 2025 -0.7, 2026 -0.8; QLD +0.1/+0.1; IEF 2022 -2.7. Attribution: the leveraged-sleeve sim understates real by 0.7 (F2) / 1.0 (F3) pp/yr; the bond synthetic overstates by 0.14-0.16pp/yr.

claims.claim: The TLT synthetic understates rate-shock risk, which strengthens the case for IEF over TLT.
claims.evidence: TLT real minus synthetic: 2022 -5.3pp, 2020 +4.5pp (TE 5.2%). Over 2010-03..freeze: F2-TLT real maxDD -37.5% vs sim -32.8%; F3-TLT -40.7% vs -36.3%; F2-IEF real -24.0%.

claims.claim: Current state (2026-11-17): both F2 and F3 are risk-off at 85% IEF + 15% gold. Out-of-sample since the freeze, F2 lost less than F3.
claims.evidence: NDX 27,002 vs EMA-100 28,968 (-6.8%; needs about +7.3% to re-enter at a Friday close); vol20 35.5%, er20 0.26. OOS Jul25-Nov17: 1x vt.30 -4.1%, F2 -6.0%, F3 -9.0%. On re-entry at today's vol: F2 QLD weight 0.72 (0.36 in chop), F3 TQQQ 0.48.

result.current_read: As of 2026-11-17 the strategy is risk-off in both the 2x and 3x versions: target 85% IEF + 15% physical gold, no QLD or TQQQ. NDX is 27,002, 6.8% below its EMA-100 (28,968), and has been below it since about mid-October. It would need about +7% to re-enter at a Friday close. vol20 is 35.5%, so on re-entry F2 would hold only 0.72 in QLD (0.36 if still choppy) and F3 0.48 in TQQQ. Out-of-sample since the 2026-07-24 freeze: 1x vt.30 -4.1%, F2 -6.0%, F3 -9.0%. Ordering by leverage is what you would expect in a falling market. The Friday rebalance did better than every other weekday again (F2 -6.0% vs -9.4% to -13.2%). Real ETFs tracked the sims within -0.2pp (F2) and -0.4pp (F3) over this window.
result.recommendation:
LEVERAGE AND VOL TARGET: keep F2, the 2x profile (QLD x min(1, 0.30/vol20), 85% engine + 15% physical gold, IEF off-leg). Do not re-optimize. Vol targets .25-.35 form a flat plateau (Calmar 0.79-0.82). Raising 2x above .35 only adds drawdown (vt.45: -30.3%). Choose 3x (F3, vt .20) only if you accept a median bootstrap maxDD of about -41% and a 1-in-20 of about -54% for its +4.4pp/yr. At matched risk it is no more efficient. Do not swap QLD for TQQQ at 2/3 weight: it gained 0.4-0.55pp/yr historically but lost 0.4pp/yr since 2023.

EXECUTION RULES FOR WEEKLY AUTOMATION:
(1) Rebalance on Fridays only. Never move to Monday, the worst day (F2 14.5%).
(2) Compute signals about 15:40-15:45 ET from live prices and send market-on-close orders (lag 1). If the run fails, trade at the next close: one day late costs about 0.2pp/yr averaged over weekdays (1.4pp in the Friday backtest). Never trade Friday on a Thursday-close signal (F2 15.6% / -30%).
(3) On a holiday Friday, trade the last trading day of that week.
(4) Use a 2pp absolute no-trade band per sleeve, with a forced trade on every risk-on/off switch. This cuts rebalances from 50 to 19 a year and orders from 132 to 56, with no return impact.
(5) Budget about 12.5x annual turnover and keep all-in cost at or below about 5 bps per unit traded (US-listed ETFs at IBKR); each 10 bps costs about 1.5pp/yr. For European/UCITS products that trade only in European hours, compute on the Friday US close and trade Monday (lag-2 economics: F2 18.3% / -25.1% IS).
(6) Keep IEF, not TLT.
(7) Set expectations from timing-luck-free numbers: about 17% CAGR / -28% maxDD (F2 tranche, in-sample), bootstrap median maxDD about -31%, 1-in-20 about -42%, before costs and taxes. Treat the roughly 2.5pp Friday premium as an unexplained calendar effect to monitor. Paper-trade first.
caveats: The Friday advantage is a calendar effect. It is significant in-sample (p about 0.002, both halves, 29/39 years) and held OOS, and there is a plausible weekend / turnaround-Tuesday mechanism, but it was never designed into the strategy and could fade. That is why planning should use the tranche numbers.
The pre-close (15:45 ET) signal approximation behind lag 1 was not tested: the panel has no intraday prices. lag 1 vs lag 2 bracket the realistic outcomes, including trading at the Monday open.

maxDD is a single-path statistic. Changing only 75 rebalance days (mark_wk) moves F3's maxDD by 2.6pp. Matched-maxDD comparisons on the realized path are fragile, so the bootstrap and tranche comparisons should carry more weight.

Before ETF inception the leveraged sleeves are simulated from the NDX price index (no dividends, no swap spread). The IEF/TLT synthetics are calibrated in-sample on 2002-2026 and understate rate-shock losses (2022 IEF -2.7pp, TLT -5.3pp). In the current high-rate regime real TQQQ trails its sim by about 0.7-0.8pp/yr.
OOS is only 81 trading days (one decline episode); nothing was chosen with post-freeze data.

432 distinct backtests were run: 18 core grid, 210 + 75 frontier-mapping fine-grid points, plus lag/weekday/band/cost/data-version checks. No grid winner is proposed; the incumbents are kept, so the 0.07-0.15 Calmar selection cost applies to any grid point cherry-picked from these tables.

The $1/order fixed-fee figure is an assumed IBKR Pro fixed minimum, used only for illustration; check actual broker pricing. Whether any European venue lets UCITS products trade at the US close was not verified.
Taxes, the US estate-tax situs issue for US-listed ETFs above $60k, and issuer risk of European 3x ETPs are not modelled here. They point the same way (toward 2x) but are outside this dimension.

verifications.lens: INTEGRITY (lookahead, data alignment/splicing, cost/turnover, spec fidelity, reproduction)

verdicts.reason: All grid numbers reproduce exactly. The rerun matched all 15,711 JSON leaves with 0 differences, e.g. F2 19.71%/-24.0%, qld vt.45 20.05%/-30.3%, and the Pareto set is identical. The framing 'leverage sets the DD band, vt only fine-tunes it' holds for 2x: vt .15-.35 gives DD -23.2..-25.1%, a 1.9pp range. It does not hold for 3x. On the coarse grid, 3x vt .15-.45 spans -29.1..-43.8% (14.7pp; .15-.35 alone spans 8.0pp). The specialist's own fine grid takes 3x to -22.9% at vt .07, and its matched pairs take 2x to -29.9% at vt .44, so the 2x and 3x DD bands overlap.
verdicts.corrected: 2x: vt .15-.35 moves DD only -23.2..-25.1% and CAGR caps near 20.05%. 3x: vt is the main DD lever (-22.9% at vt .07 to -43.8% at vt .45).

verdicts.reason: Every quoted number reproduces. 'Tied within about 1pp' is level-dependent and slightly generous to 3x at F2's operating risk. Bootstrap-matched (Friday): 2x leads by +1.63pp at median DD 30% (19.12 vs 17.49) and by +1.63pp at 1-in-20 DD 40% (18.85 vs 17.21). Tranche bootstrap-matched: 2x leads by +1.06pp at median DD 30% and +1.34pp at p5 DD 45%. On the tranche frontier at DD 28%, close to F2's own tranche DD of -27.7% and not reported, 2x leads by +1.45 (first crossing) to +1.93pp (envelope): 17.43 vs 15.98/15.50. The pairs at DD 25/30% are within ±0.4pp, and vol-matched within ±0.5pp. No formal test of the matched-risk gap was run, so 'statistically tied' is asserted rather than tested. It is plausible given CAGR noise, and the direction supports the 2x recommendation.
verdicts.corrected: At matched risk the gap is about -0.4..+1.9pp in 2x's favour near F2's risk level (bootstrap +1.1..+1.6pp). 3x wins only beyond 2x's reachable DD (~34.6% IS).

verdicts.reason: Reproduced exactly: F3-F2 +4.42pp [+1.83,+7.55]; exposure-cap effect +3.87pp; instrument effect +0.55pp [+0.15,+0.97] (H1 +0.63, H2 +0.48); real ETFs 2010-03..freeze +0.43pp. TQQQx2/3 and F2 have identical NDX exposure (max diff ~1e-16). The 'since 2023' figure used 2023..latest, which includes post-freeze data, but 2023-01-01..2026-07-24 gives -0.49pp (28.69% vs 29.18%), so the conclusion does not depend on OOS data.
verdicts.corrected: Instrument effect since 2023 using IS data only: -0.49pp/yr (2023..freeze); -0.41pp to 2026-11-17.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced: bootstrap median maxDD -30.9 vs -40.9%; 1-in-20 -41.8 vs -54.3%; P(DD<-50%) 0.8 vs 11.1%; P(Calmar F2>F3) 0.83. Worst day -11.0 vs -13.9% and worst 5 days -15.8 vs -20.4% (both 2000-01). Gap losses are exact arithmetic (0.85 x 2 x -20% = -34%; 0.85 x 3 x -20% = -51%). On the timing-luck-free tranche the tails are worse still. My 1000-draw paired bootstrap gives F3 median -42.5%, 1-in-20 -57.3%, P(DD<-50%) 17.2%, against F2 at -31.8% / -44.1% / 0.8%; P(Calmar F2>F3) 0.87.

The in-sample effect is real in the data. The weekday CAGRs, the bootstrap of +3.10pp [+0.98,+5.18] (p 0.0015), 29/39 years and the 189 vs 215-217 switches all reproduce. An independent year-block permutation agrees: random weekday-per-year schedules reach Friday's 19.71% in only 0.3% of 1000 draws (F2; 0.4% for F3), with mean 17.06% and sd 0.94pp. Data alignment is clean: no weekend rows, real sleeves synchronous with NDX (lag-0 corr 0.98-0.999), no stale-price patterns by weekday. However, about 60-65% of the premium comes from marginal near-EMA Friday decisions. With a 1% hysteresis (keep the prior state when |NDX/EMA-1|<1%), Fri minus tranche falls from +2.43 to +0.88pp (F2) and from +3.25 to +0.71pp (F3). Pre-close signal noise N(0,0.2%/0.4%) costs only Friday: -0.36/-0.73pp (F2) and -0.48/-1.01pp (F3), while Mon-Thu and the tranche move -0.15..+0.34pp. The OOS 'Friday best again' covers 81 days and Friday was second in both sub-windows: Jul25-Oct9 Thu +5.6 vs Fri +4.7; Oct10-Nov17 Mon -9.3 vs Fri -10.2. The Friday exit on 2026-10-16 came from a close only 0.40% below EMA-100 (29,187.6 vs 29,306.2). The claimed mechanism is weak for the Friday leg. Fri-to-Mon medians are -0.5bp (H1) and -7.1bp (H2), and H2 excluding 2008/2020 is -9.0bp. Mon-to-Tue is robust only in H2 (median +53bp; H1 +8.3bp, t 0.6), yet the Friday premium is larger in H1 (+3.8pp) than in H2 (+2.6pp).
verdicts.corrected: Friday premium over the tranche: +2.43pp in-sample at the exact close. About 1.8-2.0pp with realistic pre-close noise; about 0.8-0.9pp after excluding near-EMA (<1%) decisions. OOS and mechanism are weak support.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced exactly: tranche F2 17.29%/-27.7%/0.62/0.93 (H1 18.03, H2 16.59, OOS -10.7); F3 20.88%/-32.5%/0.64/0.88 (OOS -14.9). Fri minus tranche +2.45pp [+0.75,+4.12] and +3.28pp [+1.05,+5.56]. The tranche barely moves under pre-close noise (+0.04/-0.09pp F2), which makes it the robust planning base. The DD tails quoted for planning in recommendation (7) (-31%/-42%) come from the Friday bootstrap, not the tranche.
verdicts.corrected: Planning tails on the tranche basis: F2 median maxDD -31.6..-31.8%, 1-in-20 -43.5..-44.1% (specialist's 600-draw and my 1000-draw bootstraps).

verdicts.reason: Reproduced: F2 lag1 to lag2 19.71 to 18.28%, DD -24.0 to -25.1% (H1 -3.13pp, H2 +0.19pp). F3 24.13 to 22.24%, DD -30.0 to -35.0%. Weekday-averaged lag cost 0.165pp (F2) and 0.271pp (F3); tranche lag1 to lag2 gives 0.16 and 0.26pp. Oct-1987: F2 lag2 -16.9% vs lag1 -4.0%; 19-Oct-87 -12.6% vs +0.5%; F3 -27.2% vs -9.3%. The NDX calendar is verified: 1987-10-19 Mon -15.08%, 2008-10-13 Mon +12.58%, 2020-03-16 Mon -12.19%.

Reproduced: mark_wk F2 19.56%/-24.0% and F3 23.82%/-32.6% vs Friday 19.71/24.13; 75 differing days, all holiday-Friday weeks (mark & ~mark_wk = 0). claims.claim: LQQ applies its 2x to the USD Nasdaq-100; EUR is only the quote currency, so a USD investor carries no EUR exposure.
claims.evidence: With FX matched to the close time, the weekly loading on EURUSD is +0.117 (t 2.1). The USD-line placebo QQQ3.L shows the same +0.115, and leverage applied in EUR would give -1.0. Yahoo's FX bar dated D is about 00:00 London on D: it correlates 0.50 with DXY of D-1 vs 0.40 with DXY of D, and the 2015-01-22 ECB move appears in the 01-23 bar. Naive same-date conversion doubles the spurious loading (+0.235, t 4.1).

claims.claim: Backtesting European listings at lag 1 creates large look-ahead bias, because they close before the Friday US-close signal exists. The only honest execution is the Monday European close, pushed back on European-only holidays.
claims.evidence: Running UCITS at lag 1 instead of lag 2 adds +5.24 points/yr CAGR to F2 and +7.06 to F3, all of it spurious.

claims.claim: F2 through UCITS measured 3.2%/yr behind the US-ETF F2 over 2011-2026 and 2.1%/yr behind over 2009-2026.
The F2 gap breaks down into trading costs, a one-session delay, and a European-close interaction. The close interaction is noisy and concentrated in 2020; the instruments themselves cost about 0.
claims.evidence: A, one-session delay (US lag 2 vs lag 1): -0.36. B, instruments plus European close at the same session: -1.56 (leveraged sleeve -1.14, bonds -0.40, gold -0.01), bootstrap -1.58 [-3.54, +0.31]; the instrument-only estimate is +0.01. C, costs (15bp LQQ, 8bp CBU0/IGLN one-way): -1.28. Total -3.20. In 2020 alone B was -12.5pp. The 1x control (CNDX vs QQQ) shows -0.35%/yr [-1.40, +0.69], with -4.7pp in 2020.

claims.claim: F3 through the 3x ETP QQQ3.L measured 3.9%/yr behind the US version.
claims.evidence: 2013-01-03 to 2026-11-16. US TQQQ, lag 1: 25.88% / -27.5% / Calmar 0.94. UCITS QQQ3.L, lag 2, realistic costs: 21.97% / -31.6% / 0.70. Bootstrap -4.00% [-7.39, -0.61]. In-sample CAGR 27.46% vs 23.15%; out-of-sample -9.12% vs -6.66%. Decomposition: A -0.12, B -2.03 (leveraged sleeve -1.77), C -1.77. Instrument-only drag -0.62%/yr using last-5y gaps.

claims.claim: High turnover drives the trading-cost drag, and two thirds of it comes from chop-flag flips.
claims.evidence: The leveraged and bond sleeves each turn over about 6.6x/yr. F2 leveraged-sleeve turnover per year: chop flips (ER20 crossing 0.25, 15.8 flips/yr) 4.36, risk on/off 1.89, Aug/Sep season 0.31, vol rescaling 0.03. claims.claim: Neither cost mitigation tested works.
claims.evidence: A 5pp no-trade band barely changes turnover (6.32 to 6.29/yr) and CAGR (-0.05%, CI [-0.16, +0.04], 1988 to freeze). ER hysteresis 0.20/0.30 (pre-specified) cuts flips from 15.8 to 11.5/yr. At UCITS-level costs it improves F2 in 1988-2006 (19.72 to 20.44 CAGR) but worsens 2007-freeze (17.21 to 16.85); F3 goes +0.57 / -0.68. Bootstrap +0.17% [-1.07, +1.42]. It fails the pre-stated both-halves rule.

claims.claim: A hybrid (US 2x/3x ETF plus UCITS CBU0 and IGLN, everything traded Monday) costs about 1.1%/yr but only partly removes US-situs exposure.
If the broker withholds 30% on US ETF distributions, UCITS accumulating funds recover part of the gap.
claims.evidence: Trailing-12-month distribution yields: QLD 0.17%, TQQQ 0.91%, IEF 4.12%, TLT 4.93%, BIL 3.67%. Potential withholding drag on the US version: 0.53%/yr (F2) and 0.63%/yr (F3) if everything is withheld, or 0.02 and 0.12 if Treasury-ETF interest is exempt.

claims.claim: European on-exchange liquidity is a small fraction of the US ETFs'. The Leverage Shares 3x product is not viable.
claims.evidence: Median daily traded value over 6 months: LQQ.PA $5.6m, QQQ3.L $3.3m (its GBp line $6.7m), CBU0.L $10.5m, DTLA.L $7.6m, IB01.L $48.4m, IGLN.L $28.7m. US: QLD $392m, TQQQ $4.47bn, IEF $728m, GLD $2.98bn. 3QQQ.L: ADV $0.07m, AUM $1.9m, -4.58%/yr vs TQQQ since 2022-06.

claims.claim: Since the freeze (out-of-sample), the UCITS instruments moved in line with their US analogues.
Yahoo's European histories had serious defects, which were fixed with logged rules. The primary lines needed one fix.
claims.evidence: LQQ.PA had an unrecorded 200:1 split on 2015-01-02. LQQ.MI was x200 until 2026-07-09. On 2025-10-24 the USD NAV was printed into the EUR and GBp lines. GBp/GBP lines (EQQQ, SGLN 2011, IBTM/IBTS pre-2009) contain USD-line prices (factor about equal to GBPUSD). EURUSD has bad ticks in 2008. result.current_read: The strategy is risk-off: on 2026-11-16 NDX was 27,197 vs an EMA-100 of 29,008. In UCITS terms that means 85% CBU0.L (USD accumulating 7-10y Treasuries) plus 15% IGLN.L (physical gold ETC). Both track IEF and GLD with essentially no drag (-0.01 and +0.34%/yr full history; -1.8% vs -1.6% and -5.4% vs -5.1% since the freeze). So moving the current holdings to non-US-situs instruments costs only one-off trading. The UCITS drag appears once the strategy goes risk-on and starts flipping the leveraged sleeve about 16 times a year.
result.recommendation:
1. Above about $60k of US-situs exposure, use the 2x route: LQQ.PA + CBU0.L + IGLN.L. DTLA.L and IB01.L are viable if a TLT or bills sleeve is wanted.
2. Plan for about 2-3%/yr behind the US-ETF F2. Measured: 3.2%/yr over 2011-2026 and 2.1%/yr over 2009-2026. About 1.1-1.3 of that is European trading cost and about 0.4 is the one-session delay; the rest is noisy European-close timing. Up to about 0.5%/yr comes back if a broker would otherwise withhold 30% on US ETF distributions.
3. Do not use the 3x route. QQQ3.L is a non-UCITS ETP with issuer risk, measured -3.9%/yr, and lagged TQQQ by 1.65%/yr over the last 5 years. 3QQQ.L is not viable.
4. Execute on Monday during 14:30-16:30 London, while US markets are open, with limit orders, after converting USD to EUR for LQQ. Never backtest European closes at lag 1 (+5-7 points/yr of fake return).
5. The hybrid (US QLD + UCITS CBU0/IGLN, about -1.1%/yr) is a middle path but only partly removes US-situs exposure (average 44%, peak 85%).
6. Weigh the certain 2-3%/yr drag against the probability-weighted estate-tax exposure and alternatives (for example term-life cover sized to the liability) with a cross-border tax adviser. This is not tax advice.
7. The July planning note ('1.7-2.4%/yr') should be updated to 2.1-3.2%/yr measured for F2. The products are not the main cost: trading costs and execution timing are.
caveats: Trading costs are assumptions, not measurements: 15bp LQQ, 20bp QQQ3, 8bp CBU0/IGLN one-way, and 3bp for US. Yahoo bid/ask snapshots were stale or inverted (e.g. TQQQ bid 73.08 vs last 51.81). The Abdi-Ranaldo high/low spread estimator returned 35-107bp on US ETFs whose real spreads are about 1bp, so it was discarded. IBKR commission and FX schedules should be checked.

Component B (instruments plus European-close timing) is not individually significant: F2 95% CI [-3.54, +0.31], F3 [-5.64, +1.23]. It is dominated by 2020 (about -12.5pp in one year). F2, F3 and the 1x control share the same switch dates, so their consistency is not independent evidence.

Converting European closes to USD uses log-FX interpolated 16.5/24 between Yahoo FX bars. That bar timing (about 00:00 London) was inferred from the DXY correlation and event dates, not documented by Yahoo.

Yahoo's European data is noisy. Lines of the same product differ by 12-21% weekly tracking error, and the GBp/GBP lines contain unit and currency errors. Cleaning is rule-based and logged in ucits.json. Dist GBP-line dividend adjustments are unreliable (IBTM vs CBU0 -0.35%/yr) and IBTS.L could not be verified.

The UCITS windows are only 14-18 years (from 2009-2013), so they exclude dot-com and the GFC. The out-of-sample window is 16 weeks; the UCITS route's better OOS result (-4.65% vs -6.16%) is timing luck, not evidence.

Legal-form notes come from issuer-documentation knowledge, not Yahoo, and should be checked on each KID: LQQ is a French UCITS; QQQ3 is an Irish non-UCITS ETP; the gold products are ETCs, since gold cannot be held in a UCITS. ETP issuer and collateral risk is absent from the backtests. Yahoo gives no TER for the ETPs and ETCs, and its totalAssets currency is unspecified.
Tax figures are structural, not advice. Whether a broker applies the US interest-related-dividend exemption is unverified, and Pakistani vs UAE tax residency is still unresolved.

On-exchange volume understates European ETF liquidity, much of which trades off-exchange. Spreads on the 3x products after the close were 141-290bp, so fills on volatile Mondays could be worse than assumed.

Thirty-six strategy-level backtests were run. None was used to pick parameters: the primary mapping was fixed in advance by structure, USD line and liquidity, and both mitigations were pre-specified and rejected.

contradictions: NO NUMERIC CONTRADICTIONS FOR SHARED CONFIGURATIONS. VERDICT: oos_live and leverage_execution are right. Critic check: on Friday marks the lag-2 cost is a 1988-99 effect (Calmar F3 1.15->0.77, F2 1.37->0.97). Since 2000 it is small (F3 0.716->0.665 with CAGR +0.4pp; F2 0.650->0.627). On the 5-weekday tranche it is about zero in every era (IS F3 0.643->0.639, F2 0.625->0.606). revalidate's 0.17/0.09 is a 1989-91 single-episode artifact, as its robustness reviewer found.

FORWARD EXPECTATION. revalidate: 'plan forward Calmar ~0.7, F2 maxDD -25% to -30%'. leverage_execution: 'plan ~17%/-28%, Calmar 0.62'. The revalidate reviewer: 'grid median 0.69/0.71 is the anchor'. The defaults score 0.643/0.625 on the tranche, and since 2000 the default tranche Calmar is 0.54 (F3) / 0.48 (F2). The defensible anchor is Calmar ~0.5-0.6, below both dimensions' figures.

FRIDAY BASELINE vs TIMING-LUCK-FREE BASIS. oos_live, revalidate, rate_regime, managed_futures, overlays and analogs all benchmark on the Friday book. leverage_execution shows Friday beat the 5-weekday tranche by +2.45pp (F2) / +3.28pp (F3) a year. Critic checks (unreviewed): (a) on the tranche the OOS loss is F3 -14.9% (1.6th pct, below the tranche 5th pct of -11.5%) and F2 -10.7% (2.4th pct); single Mon-Thu phases sit at the 0.3-6.6th pct; Friday is at 8.4/9.1 only because it again beat every other phase OOS. (c) Friday was the pandas W-FRI default from the first July scripts (letf_opt.py), not chosen by comparing weekdays, and its premium is grid-wide. So the premium is mostly a property of the pre-specified day, plus a smaller part that is default-specific fitting. 'OOS loss is normal noise' holds only for the as-specified Friday book.

revised_strategy_candidates.name: 1. F2-IEF (2x Nasdaq-100 via QLD, US-listed ETFs): July rules unchanged, scanner corrected (primary)
revised_strategy_candidates.spec: Weekly decision at the Friday US close; if Friday is a holiday, use the last trading day of that week. Inputs from ^NDX daily closes: EMA-100 = ewm(span=100, adjust=False); vol20 = stdev of the last 20 daily returns x sqrt(252); ER20 = |C_t - C_t-20| / sum of the last 20 |daily changes|. Risk-on iff close > EMA-100; delete the yield-curve clause, which never changes a position. scale = min(1, 0.30/vol20), multiplied by 0.5 if the decision date falls in August or September. engine = scale if ER20 >= 0.25, else 0.5 x scale; engine = 0 when risk-off. Target weights: QLD = 0.85 x engine; IEF = 0.85 - QLD (replaces the scanner's TLT); physical gold (GLD) = 0.15 permanently.
